symptom: A script following the resolve-forward-references Placeholder Pattern (placeholder snippet, pages calling it, then create or modify of the real snippet) never ran clean twice: diff reported 'Snippet Admin.Snippet_AdminMenu: rewritten with only element $IDs changed (canonically equal)' on every run.
cause: Each run shrank the finished snippet to the placeholder (create or modify), then rebuilt it; the rebuild is reconciled against the placeholder that is now stored, so the original element $IDs cannot be carried back. The skill's own spelling, a plain create, fails outright on a second run ('snippet already exists').
insight: **A step that only exists for the first run must be a no-op on every later one: `create snippet|page … if not exists`, which the grammar and executor already supported.** Measured on 11.12.6: with if not exists, run 2 skips the placeholder, '3 documents already in sync', and diff says exec would write nothing; the reporter's create-or-modify placeholder reproduces the ID churn (the control); the skill's plain create fails on run 2. No code change: the fix is the documented pattern.
